findings.evidenceJa: 満足に打ち合ってもいない
findings.governingReading: They have not even exchanged enough full blows for a proper measurement.
findings.explanation: The English says they have not exchanged blows at all, contradicting the preceding dozens of clashes.

findings.highlight: something I thought of when considering how to hit swallows
findings.evidenceJa: 思いつき、身に付いただけ
findings.governingReading: Assassin says he conceived the aim of cutting a swallow and eventually acquired the technique.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the completed, acquired technique to a thought experiment about hitting swallows.

findings.highlight: If everything is to happen at the same time, the second blow has to be slower
findings.evidenceJa: 全てが同時であるなら、[ruby text=二の太刀 o2o=1]円の軌跡はどうしても遅くなる
findings.governingReading: Both blades exist simultaneously, but the second curved path necessarily arrives later because it travels farther.
findings.explanation: The English says the second blow itself must be slower, breaking the distinction between simultaneous generation and unequal arrival time.

findings.evidenceJa: 生前では叶わなかった立ち会い
findings.governingReading: Assassin rejoices at receiving the duel he could not attain during life.
findings.explanation: The English removes the lifelong lack that makes being summoned worthwhile to him.

findings.highlight: battle someone I can fully use my secret attacks on
findings.evidenceJa: 存分に振舞える殺し合い
findings.governingReading: Assassin welcomes a fight to the death in which he can freely display his secret sword technique.
findings.explanation: A death match becomes a generic battle, and one sword technique becomes plural “attacks.”

findings.evidenceJa: 対応策がほとんどない
findings.governingReading: Knowing the technique still leaves almost no way to answer it.
findings.explanation: A near-total tactical limitation becomes an absolute impossibility.
